findings:
(a) EXCHANGE RATES: TCMB indicative rate sheet dated 26.10.2026, the latest published when checked on 27.10.2026 (https://www.tcmb.gov.tr/kurlar/today.xml): USD/TRY 49.6732 buying / 49.7627 selling; EUR/TRY 55.6539 buying / 55.7542 selling. All conversions here use the selling rates. Card and bank rates will be 1-3% worse.

LOCAL BASKET (everything on the list is available in Turkey, mostly from direnc.net; prices include 20% KDV; free shipping from 1,500 TL): 25 generic 830-point breadboards (22 + 3 spares) 1,380 TL; 6 x 25 m 24 AWG solid wire in 6 colors (150 m) 1,706 TL; 560-pc pre-formed jumper kit 262 TL; Pro'sKit 6PK-223 stripper 580 TL; 300 3-mm LEDs 174 TL; 600-pc metal-film resistor kit 143 TL; 20 x 1k + 20 x 10k SIP 8+1 networks ~204 TL; 200 x 100 nF MLCC 406 TL (ceramic discs 198 TL); 30 electrolytics ~38 TL; 8 DIP-8 switches 60 TL; 20 tact buttons 30 TL; 40-pin dupont ribbons (2 M-M + 1 F-M) 169 TL; ESD tweezers 59 TL; IC extractor ~200 TL (ESTIMATE). Subtotal ~5,410 TL. Adding the Sunline U202 0-30 V/0-5 A bench supply (4,958 TL) brings it to ~10,370 TL. Adding the 5 V 5 A adapter plus a 0-100 V/0-10 A panel volt-ammeter (372 + 111 = 483 TL) instead brings it to ~5,890 TL. Swapping the 24 AWG rolls for Cat6 conductors bought by the meter would save ~700-1,100 TL (ESTIMATE).

POWER RECOMMENDATION: With 100+ 74HC chips on 22 breadboards, wiring mistakes (a reversed chip, a VCC-GND short, two bus drivers fighting) are certain. A current-limited bench supply set to 5.0 V with a ~1-1.5 A limit is the cheapest insurance against burnt chips and melted breadboard contacts, and it displays current, so no separate meter is needed. It is the recommended choice if the IC and programmer budget allows. Budget alternative: the 5 V 5 A adapter + panel volt-ammeter (powered from the measured rail, ~10 mA resolution) + a resettable PTC fuse (~1.5-2 A hold) in series. Other options: the existing multimeter in series on its 10 A range for spot checks, or the INA226 module logged by the Arduino Mega. Avoid the open-frame 5 V 10 A metal SMPS unless it is properly enclosed. Feed power at several points (both ends of every rail), because MB-102 rails have noticeable contact resistance and some versions split the rails mid-board.

MB-102 CONTACT-RELIABILITY RISK: The local 830-point boards (DirencNet, Robotistan, Robolink house brands) are generic MB-102 clones, and none states its contact material. Clones vary from batch to batch: weaker springs, thinner plating, contacts permanently spread by thick leads (diodes, electrolytic and button legs, header pins), and split rails on some versions. A CPU has thousands of contacts, and one intermittent contact produces faults that look like logic or timing bugs. This is why Ben Eater-style builds use BusBoard BB830 (phosphor bronze, nickel-plated, rated 50,000 insertions, 36 V/2 A). Wisher WBU-2xx boards specify phosphor bronze/nickel, 10,000 insertions, 48 V/5 A. Mitigations: buy 10-15% spares from one batch; continuity-test every 5-hole strip and rail on arrival; never force thick leads into the IC area; prefer 22-23 AWG wire (Cat6 conductors) for a firmer grip than 24 AWG; distribute power generously and put 100 nF on every chip; mark bad strips and stop using them.

22 AWG WIRE: No Turkish retailer was found stocking true 22 AWG (0.64 mm) solid hookup wire. direnc.net sells 24 AWG (0.50 mm conductor, 1.2 mm OD) in 25 m rolls (256-299 TL) and 0.5 mm in 100 m rolls (953 TL, ~9.5 TL/m). 24 AWG works (boards accept 20-29 AWG) but grips less firmly. A cheaper, slightly thicker alternative is Cat6 U/UTP installation cable (not patch cords, which are stranded) with 100% copper (not CCA) 23 AWG (0.57-0.58 mm) solid conductors. Nexans 305 m 23 AWG 0.58 mm 100% copper is ~8,799 TL lowest on cimri (~29 TL per meter of cable, 8 conductors). Buying 20-25 m by the meter gives 160-200 m in 4 solid + 4 striped colors (ESTIMATE 600-1,000 TL). J-Y(St)Y 0.6 mm telephone cable is another multi-color solid 0.6 mm source (no Turkish price found).

(b) CUSTOMS / IMPORT RULES (Oct 2026): Before 2026, personal postal/express parcels up to 30 EUR (cut earlier from 150 EUR) were cleared with a simplified declaration and a single flat tax: 30% for EU, 60% for non-EU, +20% for goods on ÖTV list IV. A Presidential Decision in Resmi Gazete no. 33130 (7 Jan 2026), effective 6 Feb 2026, removed that route. Since then every e-commerce order arriving by post or express courier, even one worth 1 EUR, needs a full customs declaration through a customs broker (Karar 14 Apr 2026; Habertürk 8 Jan 2026; Türkiye Gazetesi 6 Feb 2026). The buyer pays the broker fee, handling/inspection fees, customs duty per the tariff, and 20% KDV on the CIF value (+ÖTV if applicable). News sites still quote 30%/60% (+20% ÖTV) rates, and sources disagree on whether those flat rates now apply only to medicines and food supplements up to 1,500 EUR. Either way, fixed costs dominate. The 2026 customs-broker minimum fee tariff (RG 33123, 30 Dec 2025, in force 1 Jan 2026) puts an air-import declaration at roughly 3,300 TL (third-party figure, not verified against the official table). In a documented case (Karar, 14 Apr 2026), a 770 TL item arriving via PTT produced 3,984 TL brokerage + 1,908 TL inspection + ~4,500 TL taxes, about 10,400 TL in total.
STUDENT EXCEPTION ('MODEL' exemption code; Ministry of Trade circular of 30 Jan 2026, in force 6 Feb 2026; NTV and Türkiye Gazetesi 6 Feb 2026; still referenced by Dünya on 19 Oct 2026): non-commercial models and samples for R&D or education (PCBs, electronic components, sensors, chips) can be cleared by the courier on a simplified declaration (Basitleştirilmiş Gümrük Beyannamesi). Conditions: each shipment at most 30 EUR; at most 5 shipments (taşıma senedi) per person per calendar month; documents are the TCKN, proof of enrollment, and a university letter confirming project use. News sources do not clearly state the tax treatment (true 'numune' samples are duty-exempt), and customs can refuse if conditions are not met. Useful for a few rare ICs, not for bulk consumables.
Distributor terms: Mouser Turkey uses FCA, collects duties, taxes and customs fees on delivery, and ships most orders over 60 EUR free (mouser.com.tr text in search results). DigiKey showed USD prices, and import charges are the buyer's. Both ship from the US (non-EU origin).
ADVICE: Buy everything on this list locally. It is cheaper than DigiKey/Mouser even before customs: a BB830 is USD 19.73 at DigiKey (~982 TL) versus 55 TL for a local MB-102. Importing 22 BB830s: DigiKey 25 x USD 15.17 = ~18,880 TL + KDV/duty + broker, ESTIMATE ~26,000 TL landed; Mouser EU 22 x 8.56 EUR = ~10,500 TL, ESTIMATE ~16,000-18,000 TL landed. Neither fits a 30,000 TL total budget. Small AliExpress/LCSC orders are no longer worthwhile because of the ~4,000-6,000 TL clearing overhead per parcel. If an import is unavoidable, consolidate into one order, use the MODEL route with a department letter for parcels of 30 EUR or less, or ask the university BAP/purchasing office to import for the project. On AliExpress/Trendyol/Amazon TR, watch for 'Yurtdışından gönderilir' / 'Global satıcı' and only accept offers marked 'Gümrük vergileri dahil' (DDP).

(c) RELIABLE BREADBOARD BRANDS IN TURKEY: No Turkish retailer was found stocking BusBoard BB830, Global Specialties, 3M/Twin Industries, K&H or Elenco. direnc.net, robotistan and robolinkmarket sell unbranded MB-102 clones under house names (DirencNet, Robotistan, Robolink; Robotistan's Marxlow BB-301 is out of stock). Elektrovadi lists WISHER (Taiwan; WBU-2xx: phosphor-bronze/nickel contacts, 10,000 insertions) as a brand filter, but its JavaScript-rendered listing could not be read; check it in a browser or by phone. TME (Poland, ships to Turkey) stocks Wisher WBU-202. Known-good brands internationally: BusBoard BB830 (best), Wisher WBU, Global Specialties, 3M/Twin Industries, K&H. The best local signal is the direnc.net single board's 4.8/5 from 19 reviews. Practical plan: local MB-102 boards + spares + an incoming continuity test. If ICs are imported anyway in one consolidated order, adding 2-3 BB830s for the 12.6 MHz VGA pixel pipeline is a reasonable splurge.

STOCK CAVEATS: direnc.net search listings sometimes disagree with product pages on stock (560-pc and 140-pc jumper kits); confirm in the cart. Robotistan's own breadboards, its 140/500-pc jumper kits and its 30 V/5 A supplies were sold out on 27 Oct 2026. No IC extractor was found at direnc.net or robotistan (price is an ESTIMATE). Pages for Elektrovadi, Ozdisan, Akakçe, n11, cimri, TME and Mouser were blocked or JS-rendered, so those are not price-checked.
